analysis.title: The Day Ahead - North America, For Tuesday, November 3, 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 fell 0.51% to 7,541.55 and Nasdaq fell 1.07% to 25,164.32 as tech selling accelerated on AI-rally concerns. The Dow rose 0.41% to 51,983.98.

Oil fell about 8% on hopes of a US-Iran peace deal. Brent fell 8.40% to $103.90 and WTI fell 7.97% to $95.82. Iran said it is open to peace talks after eight months of war, and Qatari mediators are circulating a draft proposal.

Treasury yields: the 10-year yield was 4.9063%, the 2-year 4.5916% and the 30-year about 5.28%. Longer-dated yields fell with oil. The market still expects a December Fed rate hike, though the odds have eased in recent sessions.
Spot gold rose 1.87% to $3,946.50 an ounce after Friday's 3.6% drop took it to its lowest since October 2025.

Marvell will buy Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion including debt. The price is $1,132 per share, a 23.9% premium to the October 28 unaffected close, for an equity value of $102.54 billion. Lumentum holders get 4.5 Marvell shares per share and about 33% of the combined company. The termination fee is $5.8 billion. Lumentum fell 18.76% and Marvell fell 12.99% on the day.

Anthropic's amended IPO filing shows Q3 net loss of $23.29B versus $66.3B in Q2, and revenue of $16.96B versus $11.56B. Q3 operating loss was $567M versus operating income of $974M in Q2. Some investors value the company at about $1.5T, down from about $2T.

Oracle plans to raise $20B through bond and share sales. It had $125.34B in notes payable and borrowings as of August 31, against fiscal 2026 revenue of $67.36B. Alphabet is selling €6B of bonds in seven tranches with demand just over €17B.

October's AI and tech selloff is testing the rotation into other equity sectors. Disappointing results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel hit the AI trade. The S&P 500 is down about 4% from its peak and the Nasdaq about 10%.

US midterm elections are on November 3. The results could affect investor views on AI spending, debt ceiling talks and corporate scrutiny. Morgan Stanley strategists say the correction that began in June is in its final innings.
Data this week: factory orders, durable goods and JOLTS today, ADP and ISM services Wednesday, jobless claims Thursday, October payrolls Friday (consensus 65,000, prior 29,000, unemployment 4.2%).
The ISM manufacturing PMI rose to 55.5 in October from 54.5 in September. Production rose 2.3 points to 59. Input prices stayed high from energy costs tied to the Iran war.
Binance customers have withdrawn a net $4.72B since it reopened after a hack that stole about $6.3B of crypto.

Marriott raised its 2026 RevPAR growth forecast to 4.5%-5% from 3%-3.5%. Q3 adjusted EPS was $3.02 versus the $2.84 estimate. Estee Lauder raised its fiscal 2027 guidance, and Q1 adjusted EPS was $0.72 versus the $0.51 estimate.
Tesla's October European registrations rose 248% in Sweden, 131% in Norway, 271% in Spain, 186% in Portugal and 94% in Italy, helped by easy year-ago comparisons and higher fuel prices.
Canada's manufacturing PMI fell to 49.6 in October from 51.5, the first contraction in 2026. The TSX rose 0.51% while energy stocks fell 4.84%.

market_movers.rationale: Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum at $1,132 per share in stock. Lumentum closed at $683.01, down 18.76%.
Marvell fell 12.99% to $170.88 after announcing the all-stock Lumentum purchase, which gives Lumentum holders about 33% of the combined company.
Ciena fell 11.42% to $284.08 in the tech selloff.
IDEXX rose 21.95% to $672.19, the top S&P 500 gainer.
AMD reports after the close. Analysts expect revenue growth from CPU demand in AI servers.
Investors expect Repatha sales to drive a Q3 beat. A failed Novartis Lp(a) trial raised questions about Amgen's olpasiran.
Marriott raised its full-year RevPAR forecast and beat Q3 EPS estimates.
Estee Lauder raised annual forecasts and beat Q1 EPS and sales estimates.

sector_views.rationale: Becci McKinley-Rowe of Reuters Open Interest argues that AI adopters such as healthcare may be the next wave of AI winners after the chip and infrastructure makers.
Canadian energy stocks fell 4.84% as Brent dropped on US-Iran peace hopes. This is a market move, not a bank call.

earnings_insights: Pfizer reports Q3 before market open. LSEG consensus EPS is $0.73 (Smart Estimate $0.75), year-ago $0.87, revenue estimate $15,872M. Focus is on Eliquis, recently acquired drugs and obesity commentary.
AMD reports Q3 after the close. Consensus EPS is $1.95 (Smart Estimate $1.96), year-ago $1.20, revenue estimate $13,093.88M.
Amgen reports Q3 after the close. Consensus EPS is $5.79 (Smart Estimate $5.84), year-ago $5.64, revenue estimate $10,070.90M.
Super Micro Computer reports fiscal Q1 after the close. Consensus EPS is $1.23 (Smart Estimate $1.62), year-ago $0.35, revenue estimate $16,389.09M.
Marathon Petroleum reports Q3 before market open. Consensus EPS is $24.47 (Smart Estimate $25.76), year-ago $3.01, on stronger refining margins.
Booking Holdings reports Q3 after the close. Consensus EPS is $4.50 (Smart Estimate $4.53), year-ago $3.98, revenue estimate $9,548.03M.

Other reports today (consensus EPS): Apollo $2.20 BMO, AIG $1.89 AMC, Arista $1.08 AMC, Block $1.03 AMC, Eaton $3.54 BMO, Fiserv $1.72 BMO, Keurig Dr Pepper $0.62 BMO, Yum $1.49 (Smart Estimate $1.43).
Marriott reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $3.02 versus the LSEG estimate of $2.84, on revenue of about $7B versus the $6.92B estimate. It raised its 2026 RevPAR growth forecast to 4.5%-5% from 3%-3.5%.

Estee Lauder reported Q1 sales up 7% to $3.72B versus the $3.65B estimate, and adjusted EPS of $0.72 versus the $0.51 estimate. It raised fiscal 2027 organic sales growth guidance to 4%-5.5% and adjusted EPS guidance to $3.20-$3.45.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Consensus is for a rise from 0.1% in August.
Up from 54.5 in September. Manufacturing activity improved on domestic demand while input prices stayed elevated.
Poll compared with 29,000 prior. The unemployment rate is expected to stay at 4.2%.
Down from 51.5, the first sub-50 reading since December. Output fell to 48.4 and new orders to 46.5.
Down 0.14% as oil and yields fell.

crypto_views: Binance customers withdrew a net $4.72B after hackers stole about $6.3B from the exchange, which may be the largest financial heist on record.
risk_factors: Further AI-linked selling, with investors questioning whether returns justify heavy AI spending and the financing it requires.
A reversal in the US-Iran talks would lift oil and inflation pressure again.
Midterm results could affect AI spending, debt ceiling negotiations and scrutiny of companies.
A Nasdaq drawdown deeper than 10% could test the broader market, which has held up better than tech in October.
Higher energy costs are feeding into inflation and a possible December Fed hike.
vol_and_positioning: Oil is reacting with extreme sensitivity to Middle East headlines, per UBS's Giovanni Staunovo. December WTI tested $105 on Friday and is now below $100.
Fed funds futures still price a December rate hike, though the odds have eased over the last couple of sessions, per Zaner Metals' Peter Grant.
geopolitical: Iran signaled openness to peace talks after eight months of war with the US and Israel. Qatari mediators are circulating a draft proposal, and a follow-up meeting is possible.
US midterm elections on November 3 will decide whether Democrats take control of Congress from Trump's Republican Party.
Automakers are urging Congress to pass a permanent ban on Chinese vehicles in the post-election session.
Cheam First Nation filed a court challenge to the fast-tracked review of the Pacific Link oil pipeline in British Columbia.
Tariffs and the Iran war are cited as drivers of inflation and voter discontent.

tension_points.bull_case: This may be another buy-the-dip episode. The S&P 500 is only about 4% below its peak, the broader market held up better than tech in October, and Morgan Stanley says the correction is in its final innings.
tension_points.bear_case: Disappointing Alphabet, Amazon and Intel results, heavy AI financing needs and doubts about returns are pressuring tech. A Nasdaq drop deeper than 10% could break the rotation that has supported broader indexes and deepen the slowdown.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A more severe pullback in the AI trade that the broader market cannot absorb.

tension_points.bull_case: Iran's openness to peace talks pushed oil down about 8%, which eases inflation pressure and lowers yields and December rate hike odds.
tension_points.bear_case: Oil remains highly sensitive to headlines, and a breakdown in talks could send it back above $100, where December WTI traded on Friday.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A collapse of the US-Iran talks, with December WTI back near the $105 level it tested on Friday.

theme_stances.key_argument: Disappointing big-tech results and financing worries are testing the AI rally and the rotation into other sectors.
theme_stances.evidence: Disappointing results from Alphabet, Amazon and Intel dealt the latest blow

theme_stances.key_argument: Oil fell sharply on hopes for a peace deal, which tempered inflation concerns and lowered yields.
theme_stances.evidence: Oil is sliding down today so you could see yields come down

theme_stances.key_argument: The next wave of AI market gains may belong to adopters, with healthcare well placed.
